PD-14 Marker-last publication protocol: freeze one request, timestamps, transaction ID, budget IDs, exact payload/control bytes, all hashes, and expected pointer before effects; reserve RM-011 resources; acquire the run authority; verify root ownership, legacy-root identity, namespace, aliases, current-to-genesis lineage, idempotency, and expected revision/manifest/pointer; exclusive-create and fsync transaction and every payload; reread and validate them; write and fsync manifest; reread manifest and payload inventory; for product_terminal write and fsync lifecycle metadata payload before writing completion.json as the last revision-local data artifact; reread marker/manifest/payload; atomically replace current.json after final CAS; reconcile the new pointer; then exactly settle the durable budget binding. The reader withholds terminal status until settlement verification succeeds.

PD-15 Reader protocol: parse pointer version before model dispatch without permissive fallback; read pointer, selected immutable revision, manifest, all required payloads, optional marker, lifecycle binding, and budget binding; verify run/root/revision/transaction/path/version/hash/size/schema/inventory/provenance/state matrices; reread pointer and require byte identity. Return complete old or complete new current only. Preserve and verify all reachable prior revisions current-to-genesis. Do not scan arbitrary directories to guess completion and do not silently adopt orphan or legacy data.

PD-16 Lock/wait/lease/stale policy: retain P2-012A same-process registry plus stable one-byte kernel authority as the only write authority. Product default is one nonblocking acquisition attempt, wait timeout zero, no sleep/backoff, and no automatic retry. AuthorityLease means the lifetime of the held Windows msvcrt byte-range or POSIX flock kernel lock; there is no clock-expiring authority lease, heartbeat renewal, or lock stealing in P2-012B. Advisory acquired UTC/PID/owner metadata never grants or revokes authority. Stale is diagnostic only after exclusive kernel acquisition proves no live cooperating holder and stored process/boot evidence, when available, is non-live; unavailable identity evidence yields manual reconciliation, not stale. RecoveryClaimV1 remains metadata-only, single-winner under the acquired authority, and never moves, deletes, repairs, publishes, or quarantines an orphan.

PD-17 Concurrency, ordering, and idempotency: cooperating writers serialize on one authority and use expected revision, previous manifest hash, expected pointer hash, and a stable pointer reread. Last-write-wins is forbidden. Same transaction ID plus identical frozen request/payload/budget hashes returns the already committed outcome after full verification; any differing reuse is idempotency_conflict. Deterministic payload/inventory/tool order is content-defined and independent of task completion timing. A pointer CAS loser leaves an immutable unreferenced revision and returns reconciliation_required. No automatic parallel execution or automatic retry is enabled in the ordinary product path.

PD-18 Crash/status boundaries: faults before revision publication may leave staging residue; after immutable rename and before pointer replace may leave an unreferenced revision; during pointer replace may be effect_unknown; after pointer and before budget settlement produces incomplete plus budget_settlement_failed until exact reconciliation. Marker-only, manifest-only, terminal state-only, missing marker, missing required payload, invalid schema, hash mismatch, corrupt pointer, and unsupported version are never completed. A verified prior current revision remains readable when a later orphan exists. Fault injection covers every file create/write/flush/fsync/close/reread/rename, marker, final CAS, pointer replace, directory sync, lock acquire/release, budget reserve/settle, migration inventory, and lifecycle evaluation boundary.

PD-19 v1 read-only adapter: legacy_migration.py recognizes only the exact .poker-deliberation-run bytes v1 followed by LF, the existing portable run-ID grammar and confinement rules, known fixed artifact names/directories, strict current CaseInput/FinalReport/state/approval/tool/evidence schemas where a schema exists, duplicate-free JSON, UTF-8, and bounded sizes. Missing v1 integrity evidence remains an explicit missing guarantee and its read status is legacy_unverified.

PD-20 Copy-only migration: require an explicit source_quiescence_acknowledged=true input, compute the canonical source inventory from relative path, media/schema observation, byte size, and SHA-256 before copy, copy admitted bytes into a distinct destination run ID in the dedicated product revision root, reread the source and require the identical inventory after copy, and publish publication_kind legacy_copy with status legacy_unverified, no completion marker, resume_eligible=false, and LegacySourceBindingV2. The source root/run is never renamed, linked, locked by invented authority, rewritten, repaired, or deleted. A changed source returns migration_source_changed and leaves only a destination orphan. The idempotency identity is the tuple of source-root identity hash, source-run hash, source-inventory hash, and destination run ID; same identity replays, any collision conflicts. Old unknown and all future versions are refused.

PD-21 RM-011 reservation/settlement: terminal_store.py composes the completed P2-011B DurableBudgetStore API without changing its schemas. Before any product revision mutation, reserve execution_class local_free, external cost zero, concurrency_slots one, active_runtime_ns equal to the verified remaining allowance, artifact_bytes equal to the largest exact planned payload/control file, and run_bytes equal to the exact new persistent-byte delta; provider/tool/retry/cost fields are zero. P2-012A physical peak quota, including temp/orphan/control bytes, remains independent, and either stricter refusal wins. Lock acquisition, writes, rereads, verification, marker, CAS, and reconciliation elapsed time are included in the post-pointer actual settlement. No-effect prewrite failure uses exact release_no_effect. Pointer-published uncertainty settles or latches effect_unknown and cannot be blindly released.

PD-22 Cross-root completion rule: the frozen BudgetSettlementBindingV2 IDs and reservation hash are in RunManifestV2 and their hash is in CompletionMarkerV2. After pointer publication, settle exactly once with actual runtime/byte values, result_sha256 equal to the verified pointer SHA-256, and effect_evidence_sha256 equal to the verified completion-marker SHA-256 for product_terminal or the verified manifest SHA-256 otherwise. The verified reader queries the bound dedicated budget root and requires the exact successful or explicit terminal-failure settlement, matching policy/run/operation/permit/settlement IDs and hashes. Missing, overrun, conflicting, effect_unknown, or reconciliation-required settlement withholds terminal status. Exact settlement replay is allowed; storage publication is not rerun.

PD-23 Cancellation and external effects: cancelled requires acknowledged cooperative cancellation evidence and a terminal marker; cancel_unconfirmed records no hard-stop claim and maps to failure. A live/unacknowledged worker, callable exception after possible effect, remote ambiguity, or pointer/settlement ambiguity is effect_unknown and non-retryable without authoritative reconciliation. P2-012B does not implement process-tree kill, remote cancellation, OS CPU/memory/output isolation, external provider, external solver, or RM-028 evidence implementation.

PD-14 Marker-last publication protocol: freeze one request, timestamps, transaction ID, budget IDs, exact payload/control bytes, all hashes, and expected pointer before effects; reserve RM-011 resources; acquire the run authority; verify root ownership, legacy-root identity, namespace, aliases, current-to-genesis lineage, idempotency, and expected revision/manifest/pointer; exclusive-create and fsync transaction and every payload; reread and validate them; write and fsync manifest; reread manifest and payload inventory; for product_terminal write and fsync lifecycle metadata payload before writing completion.json as the last revision-local data artifact; reread marker/manifest/payload; atomically replace current.json after final CAS; reconcile the new pointer; then exactly settle the durable budget binding. The reader withholds terminal status until settlement verification succeeds.

PD-15 Reader protocol: parse pointer version before model dispatch without permissive fallback; read pointer, selected immutable revision, manifest, all required payloads, optional marker, lifecycle binding, and budget binding; verify run/root/revision/transaction/path/version/hash/size/schema/inventory/provenance/state matrices; reread pointer and require byte identity. Return complete old or complete new current only. Preserve and verify all reachable prior revisions current-to-genesis. Do not scan arbitrary directories to guess completion and do not silently adopt orphan or legacy data.

PD-16 Lock/wait/lease/stale policy: retain P2-012A same-process registry plus stable one-byte kernel authority as the only write authority. Product default is one nonblocking acquisition attempt, wait timeout zero, no sleep/backoff, and no automatic retry. AuthorityLease means the lifetime of the held Windows msvcrt byte-range or POSIX flock kernel lock; there is no clock-expiring authority lease, heartbeat renewal, or lock stealing in P2-012B. Advisory acquired UTC/PID/owner metadata never grants or revokes authority. Stale is diagnostic only after exclusive kernel acquisition proves no live cooperating holder and stored process/boot evidence, when available, is non-live; unavailable identity evidence yields manual reconciliation, not stale. RecoveryClaimV1 remains metadata-only, single-winner under the acquired authority, and never moves, deletes, repairs, publishes, or quarantines an orphan.

PD-17 Concurrency, ordering, and idempotency: cooperating writers serialize on one authority and use expected revision, previous manifest hash, expected pointer hash, and a stable pointer reread. Last-write-wins is forbidden. Same transaction ID plus identical frozen request/payload/budget hashes returns the already committed outcome after full verification; any differing reuse is idempotency_conflict. Deterministic payload/inventory/tool order is content-defined and independent of task completion timing. A pointer CAS loser leaves an immutable unreferenced revision and returns reconciliation_required. No automatic parallel execution or automatic retry is enabled in the ordinary product path.

PD-18 Crash/status boundaries: faults before revision publication may leave staging residue; after immutable rename and before pointer replace may leave an unreferenced revision; during pointer replace may be effect_unknown; after pointer and before budget settlement produces incomplete plus budget_settlement_failed until exact reconciliation. Marker-only, manifest-only, terminal state-only, missing marker, missing required payload, invalid schema, hash mismatch, corrupt pointer, and unsupported version are never completed. A verified prior current revision remains readable when a later orphan exists. Fault injection covers every file create/write/flush/fsync/close/reread/rename, marker, final CAS, pointer replace, directory sync, lock acquire/release, budget reserve/settle, migration inventory, and lifecycle evaluation boundary.

PD-19 v1 read-only adapter: legacy_migration.py recognizes only the exact .poker-deliberation-run bytes v1 followed by LF, the existing portable run-ID grammar and confinement rules, known fixed artifact names/directories, strict current CaseInput/FinalReport/state/approval/tool/evidence schemas where a schema exists, duplicate-free JSON, UTF-8, and bounded sizes. It performs no mkdir, temp write, normalization rewrite, repair, append, state transition, resume, or implicit migration. Missing v1 integrity evidence remains an explicit missing guarantee and its read status is legacy_unverified.

PD-20 Copy-only migration: require an explicit source_quiescence_acknowledged=true input, compute the canonical source inventory from relative path, media/schema observation, byte size, and SHA-256 before copy, copy admitted bytes into a distinct destination run ID in the dedicated product revision root, reread the source and require the identical inventory after copy, and publish publication_kind legacy_copy with status legacy_unverified, no completion marker, resume_eligible=false, and LegacySourceBindingV2. The source root/run is never renamed, linked, locked by invented authority, rewritten, repaired, or deleted. A changed source returns migration_source_changed and leaves only a destination orphan. The idempotency identity is the tuple of source-root identity hash, source-run hash, source-inventory hash, and destination run ID; same identity replays, any collision conflicts. Old unknown and all future versions are refused.

PD-21 RM-011 reservation/settlement: terminal_store.py composes the completed P2-011B DurableBudgetStore API without changing its schemas. Before any product revision mutation, reserve execution_class local_free, external cost zero, concurrency_slots one, active_runtime_ns equal to the verified remaining allowance, artifact_bytes equal to the largest exact planned payload/control file, and run_bytes equal to the exact new persistent-byte delta; provider/tool/retry/cost fields are zero. P2-012A physical peak quota, including temp/orphan/control bytes, remains independent, and either stricter refusal wins. Lock acquisition, writes, rereads, verification, marker, CAS, and reconciliation elapsed time are included in the post-pointer actual settlement. No-effect prewrite failure uses exact release_no_effect. Pointer-published uncertainty settles or latches effect_unknown and cannot be blindly released.

PD-22 Cross-root completion rule: the frozen BudgetSettlementBindingV2 IDs and reservation hash are in RunManifestV2 and their hash is in CompletionMarkerV2. After pointer publication, settle exactly once with actual runtime/byte values, result_sha256 equal to the verified pointer SHA-256, and effect_evidence_sha256 equal to the verified completion-marker SHA-256 for product_terminal or the verified manifest SHA-256 otherwise. The verified reader queries the bound dedicated budget root and requires the exact successful or explicit terminal-failure settlement, matching policy/run/operation/permit/settlement IDs and hashes. Missing, overrun, conflicting, effect_unknown, or reconciliation-required settlement withholds terminal status. Exact settlement replay is allowed; storage publication is not rerun.

PD-15 Reader protocol: parse pointer version before model dispatch without permissive fallback; read pointer, selected immutable revision, manifest, all required payloads, optional marker, lifecycle binding, and budget binding; verify run/root/revision/transaction/path/version/hash/size/schema/inventory/provenance/state matrices; reread pointer and require byte identity. Advisory acquired UTC/PID/owner metadata never grants or revokes authority. Stale is diagnostic only after exclusive kernel acquisition proves no live cooperating holder and stored process/boot evidence, when available, is non-live; unavailable identity evidence yields manual reconciliation, not stale. RecoveryClaimV1 remains metadata-only, single-winner under the acquired authority, and never moves, deletes, repairs, publishes, or quarantines an orphan.

PD-17 Concurrency, ordering, and idempotency: cooperating writers serialize on one authority and use expected revision, previous manifest hash, expected pointer hash, and a stable pointer reread. Last-write-wins is forbidden. Same transaction ID plus identical frozen request/payload/budget hashes returns the already committed outcome after full verification; any differing reuse is idempotency_conflict. Deterministic payload/inventory/tool order is content-defined and independent of task completion timing. A pointer CAS loser leaves an immutable unreferenced revision and returns reconciliation_required. No automatic parallel execution or automatic retry is enabled in the ordinary product path.

PD-18 Crash/status boundaries: faults before revision publication may leave staging residue; after immutable rename and before pointer replace may leave an unreferenced revision; during pointer replace may be effect_unknown; after pointer and before budget settlement produces incomplete plus budget_settlement_failed until exact reconciliation. milestone_contract.scope: Completion marker, verified reader/status mapping, migration, and lifecycle hooks.

acceptance_criteria: Immutable revision artifacts preserve every prior verified revision; a terminal marker is written last inside the revision and an atomic current pointer is published only after readers verify run ID, manifest, payload inventory, sizes, and hashes.
item_contract.objective: Distinguish completed, incomplete, corrupt, unsupported, and resumable runs with integrity evidence.

acceptance_criteria: AC-01: The canonical RM-012 item_contract and P2-012B milestone_contract are byte-for-value identical to roadmap_status.json at the approved base; P2-012A schema fields and meanings remain unchanged.

AC-02: terminal_models.py owns strict frozen extra-forbid RunManifestV2, CompletionMarkerV2, RunCurrentPointerV2, RunReadStatus, verified-read values, legacy-source and budget-settlement bindings, and redacted structured failure values; terminal_canonical.py owns their canonical bytes, domain-separated SHA-256, version dispatch, inventory ordering, and closed cross-field validation.

AC-03: A product terminal revision writes and verifies every payload and RunManifestV2 before writing completion.json as the final revision-local data artifact; failed, cancelled, and cancel_unconfirmed terminal revisions require the same marker protocol as succeeded revisions.

AC-04: terminal_store.py rereads and validates payload, manifest, marker, inventory, lineage, lifecycle binding, and expected RM-011 settlement binding before replacing current.json by expected-previous-pointer CAS; a CAS loss leaves an identifiable orphan and never changes the prior verified current revision.

AC-05: RunReadStatus deterministically distinguishes in_progress, approval_required, succeeded, failed, cancelled, cancel_unconfirmed, incomplete, corrupt, unsupported_version, and legacy_unverified; only fully verified succeeded maps to public FinalReport.run_status completed and CLI exit 0.

AC-06: The read-only flat-v1 adapter never writes the source and never promotes it to completed; copy-only migration writes a distinct destination run, preserves an exact legacy source inventory binding and missing-guarantee list, and leaves the destination legacy_unverified and non-resumable.

AC-07: Migration requires a valid v1 sentinel and run ID, explicit source-quiescent acknowledgement, identical canonical source inventory hashes before and after copy, deterministic idempotency identity, distinct source and destination IDs, and fail-closed rejection of old-unknown or future schema versions.

AC-08: Product publication reuses the stable process/kernel authority and portable path identity from P2-012A, uses nonblocking zero-wait acquisition by default, never steals a live lock, treats time-based lease expiry as disabled, and permits only metadata recovery claims under an acquired exclusive authority on Windows msvcrt or POSIX flock adapters.

AC-09: Before any product revision filesystem mutation, the RM-011 durable budget root atomically reserves one concurrency slot, remaining active-runtime allowance, exact projected persistent run-byte delta, and maximum single-artifact bytes; after pointer publication it records an exact idempotent settlement bound to the pointer and marker hashes, and the reader withholds terminal status until that settlement verifies.

AC-10: RunManifestV2 lineage heads match approval, ContextEnvelope scalar correlation, phase, execution, tool, report, and event evidence in admitted payloads; raw ContextEnvelope, canonical context payload, AgentContext, provider payload, secrets, tracebacks, or unrestricted error text are not newly persisted.

AC-11: Every admitted ToolResult round-trips its contract version, numeric exactness, exact/approximation metadata, verification observations, model qualifier, seed/sample/iteration/stopping data, warnings, and reproduction metadata without inventory-order changes; solver_status remains unavailable and no solver-free GTO, equilibrium, exploitability, or exact-range claim is created.

AC-12: lifecycle_hooks.py invokes only the P2-027A pure policy, uses CompletionMarkerV2.published_at as the verified-terminal retention anchor, persists only bounded lifecycle metadata admitted before the marker, maps incomplete/corrupt/orphan subjects to candidate outcomes, and performs no scan, move, quarantine, deletion, encryption, receipt, tombstone, or secure erase.

AC-13: Every read, migration, publish, and recovery path rejects traversal, absolute/drive/URI/ADS forms, non-NFC or case aliases, Windows reserved names, symlink/reparse/hardlink escape, cross-run substitution, duplicate JSON keys, hash/algorithm/version downgrade, mixed namespace, and source/inventory swap before trusting status.

AC-14: Existing Orchestrator constructor positional parameters and current keyword parameters, run/resume/load_report/report_path signatures, CaseInput, ToolRequest, ToolResult, FinalReport fields, CLI command names, and exit codes 0/2/3 remain source-compatible; new dependencies are keyword-only and flat-v1 source bytes are never modified.

AC-15: Ordinary product execution remains serial with zero automatic retry and no unapproved parallel provider/tool execution; effect_unknown, cancellation without acknowledgement, lock ambiguity, budget settlement ambiguity, and durability uncertainty require reconciliation and never become success.

AC-16: product_integrated_durable_run changes from planned to implemented only when the ordinary run/resume/show/load_report/report_path product path defaults to the verified V2 reader/writer, v1 is read-only, migration is copy-only, and all exact gates pass; immutable_revision_storage_foundation remains implemented and unrelated capabilities do not change.

PD-06 RunManifestV2 exact serialized fields, with no additional fields, are run_schema_version, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, publication_kind, run_id, revision, transaction_id, previous_revision, previous_manifest_sha256, expected_pointer_sha256, created_at, updated_at, producer_id, producer_version, framework_version, source_commit_id, tool_contract_versions, status, canonical_input_sha256, config_sha256, budget_policy_sha256, budget_binding, redaction_policy_sha256, local_data_policy_sha256, state_checkpoint_sha256, event_head_sha256, approval_lineage_head_sha256, context_lineage_head_sha256, execution_lineage_head_sha256, legacy_source, inventory_sha256, lifecycle_audit_sha256, and artifacts. publication_kind is product_checkpoint, product_terminal, or legacy_copy; status is respectively in_progress/approval_required, succeeded/failed/cancelled/cancel_unconfirmed, or legacy_unverified. PD-09 RunCurrentPointerV2 exact serialized fields, with pointer_sha256 derived and never serialized, are schema_version, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, publication_kind, run_id, revision, transaction_id, revision_relative_path, status, manifest_sha256, inventory_sha256, completion_marker_sha256, and published_at. completion_marker_sha256 is nonnull exactly for product_terminal. revision_relative_path is recomputed from revision and transaction_id. PD-10 Inventory and canonical hashing: reuse PayloadInventoryEntryV1 and its admitted exact bytes, classification, source, and provenance validation. Inventory includes payload artifacts only and excludes transaction.json, manifest.json, completion.json, current.json, authority/metadata, temp, recovery claims, and lifecycle candidates outside an admitted payload. Relative paths use POSIX separators, one confined NFC segment family, unique bytewise UTF-8 order, exact media/schema/serialization tuples, exact size, and lowercase SHA-256. The required_inventory_sha256 is a separate domain hash over required inventory entries only; artifact order never changes ToolResult execution ordinal or FinalReport.tool_results order.

PD-11 RunReadStatus exact vocabulary is in_progress, approval_required, succeeded, failed, cancelled, cancel_unconfirmed, incomplete, corrupt, unsupported_version, and legacy_unverified. resume_eligible is true only for a stable verified current checkpoint with status in_progress or approval_required, a verified compatible budget state, and exact lineage; it is false for every other status. Missing current with recognizable staging/revision residue, terminal state without a marker, marker without a manifest, or an unsettled published pointer is incomplete. A previously published current pointer whose required bytes are missing or mismatched, invalid supported-version JSON/schema, run/cross-root mismatch, or hash/size/source/lineage swap is corrupt. Unknown future version is unsupported_version. A flat-v1 sentinel or legacy_copy is legacy_unverified.

PD-12 Public status mapping: stable verified succeeded alone maps to FinalReport.run_status completed. Stable verified approval_required maps to approval_required. Stable verified failed, cancelled, and cancel_unconfirmed map to failed_with_limitations with a fixed non-secret limitation code; legacy_unverified may be shown through an immutable parsed projection only as failed_with_limitations and never resumed. load_report refuses in_progress without a complete admitted report and raises a typed ProductRunError for incomplete, corrupt, or unsupported versions. No marker, manifest, state.json, report, or transition alone can produce completed.

PD-13 ProductRunFailureCode exact vocabulary is run_not_found, run_locked, lock_unavailable, run_conflict, run_incomplete, run_corrupt, unsupported_run_version, legacy_run_unverified, artifact_missing, artifact_hash_mismatch, artifact_schema_error, path_confinement_failed, link_or_reparse_detected, cross_run_mismatch, hash_algorithm_mismatch, idempotency_conflict, migration_source_changed, migration_source_busy, migration_conflict, budget_reservation_failed, budget_settlement_failed, durability_unconfirmed, effect_unknown, lifecycle_policy_failed, and internal_invariant_error. ProductRunFailureV2 exact fields are schema_version, code, stage, read_status, message_code, automatic_retry_allowed=false, retryable, reconciliation_required, filesystem_effect, domain_effect, previous_revision_effect, run_id_sha256, transaction_id, observed_revision, observed_pointer_sha256, and durability_evidence; it contains no raw path, run ID, payload excerpt, exception, traceback, secret, or unrestricted message.

PD-14 Marker-last publication protocol: freeze one request, timestamps, transaction ID, budget IDs, exact payload/control bytes, all hashes, and expected pointer before effects; reserve RM-011 resources; acquire the run authority; verify root ownership, legacy-root identity, namespace, aliases, current-to-genesis lineage, idempotency, and expected revision/manifest/pointer; exclusive-create and fsync transaction and every payload; reread and validate them; write and fsync manifest; reread manifest and payload inventory; for product_terminal write and fsync lifecycle metadata payload before writing completion.json as the last revision-local data artifact; reread marker/manifest/payload; atomically replace current.json after final CAS; reconcile the new pointer; then exactly settle the durable budget binding. The reader withholds terminal status until settlement verification succeeds.

PD-15 Reader protocol: parse pointer version before model dispatch without permissive fallback; read pointer, selected immutable revision, manifest, all required payloads, optional marker, lifecycle binding, and budget binding; verify run/root/revision/transaction/path/version/hash/size/schema/inventory/provenance/state matrices; reread pointer and require byte identity. Return complete old or complete new current only. Preserve and verify all reachable prior revisions current-to-genesis. Do not scan arbitrary directories to guess completion and do not silently adopt orphan or legacy data.

PD-16 Lock/wait/lease/stale policy: retain P2-012A same-process registry plus stable one-byte kernel authority as the only write authority. Product default is one nonblocking acquisition attempt, wait timeout zero, no sleep/backoff, and no automatic retry. AuthorityLease means the lifetime of the held Windows msvcrt byte-range or POSIX flock kernel lock; there is no clock-expiring authority lease, heartbeat renewal, or lock stealing in P2-012B. Advisory acquired UTC/PID/owner metadata never grants or revokes authority. Stale is diagnostic only after exclusive kernel acquisition proves no live cooperating holder and stored process/boot evidence, when available, is non-live; unavailable identity evidence yields manual reconciliation, not stale. RecoveryClaimV1 remains metadata-only, single-winner under the acquired authority, and never moves, deletes, repairs, publishes, or quarantines an orphan.

PD-17 Concurrency, ordering, and idempotency: cooperating writers serialize on one authority and use expected revision, previous manifest hash, expected pointer hash, and a stable pointer reread. Last-write-wins is forbidden. Same transaction ID plus identical frozen request/payload/budget hashes returns the already committed outcome after full verification; any differing reuse is idempotency_conflict. Deterministic payload/inventory/tool order is content-defined and independent of task completion timing. A pointer CAS loser leaves an immutable unreferenced revision and returns reconciliation_required. No automatic parallel execution or automatic retry is enabled in the ordinary product path.

PD-18 Crash/status boundaries: faults before revision publication may leave staging residue; after immutable rename and before pointer replace may leave an unreferenced revision; during pointer replace may be effect_unknown; after pointer and before budget settlement produces incomplete plus budget_settlement_failed until exact reconciliation. Marker-only, manifest-only, terminal state-only, missing marker, missing required payload, invalid schema, hash mismatch, corrupt pointer, and unsupported version are never completed. A verified prior current revision remains readable when a later orphan exists. Fault injection covers every file create/write/flush/fsync/close/reread/rename, marker, final CAS, pointer replace, directory sync, lock acquire/release, budget reserve/settle, migration inventory, and lifecycle evaluation boundary.

PD-19 v1 read-only adapter: legacy_migration.py recognizes only the exact .poker-deliberation-run bytes v1 followed by LF, the existing portable run-ID grammar and confinement rules, known fixed artifact names/directories, strict current CaseInput/FinalReport/state/approval/tool/evidence schemas where a schema exists, duplicate-free JSON, UTF-8, and bounded sizes. It performs no mkdir, temp write, normalization rewrite, repair, append, state transition, resume, or implicit migration. Missing v1 integrity evidence remains an explicit missing guarantee and its read status is legacy_unverified.

PD-20 Copy-only migration: require an explicit source_quiescence_acknowledged=true input, compute the canonical source inventory from relative path, media/schema observation, byte size, and SHA-256 before copy, copy admitted bytes into a distinct destination run ID in the dedicated product revision root, reread the source and require the identical inventory after copy, and publish publication_kind legacy_copy with status legacy_unverified, no completion marker, resume_eligible=false, and LegacySourceBindingV2. The source root/run is never renamed, linked, locked by invented authority, rewritten, repaired, or deleted. A changed source returns migration_source_changed and leaves only a destination orphan. The idempotency identity is the tuple of source-root identity hash, source-run hash, source-inventory hash, and destination run ID; same identity replays, any collision conflicts. Old unknown and all future versions are refused.

PD-21 RM-011 reservation/settlement: terminal_store.py composes the completed P2-011B DurableBudgetStore API without changing its schemas. Before any product revision mutation, reserve execution_class local_free, external cost zero, concurrency_slots one, active_runtime_ns equal to the verified remaining allowance, artifact_bytes equal to the largest exact planned payload/control file, and run_bytes equal to the exact new persistent-byte delta; provider/tool/retry/cost fields are zero. P2-012A physical peak quota, including temp/orphan/control bytes, remains independent, and either stricter refusal wins. Lock acquisition, writes, rereads, verification, marker, CAS, and reconciliation elapsed time are included in the post-pointer actual settlement. No-effect prewrite failure uses exact release_no_effect. Pointer-published uncertainty settles or latches effect_unknown and cannot be blindly released.

PD-22 Cross-root completion rule: the frozen BudgetSettlementBindingV2 IDs and reservation hash are in RunManifestV2 and their hash is in CompletionMarkerV2. After pointer publication, settle exactly once with actual runtime/byte values, result_sha256 equal to the verified pointer SHA-256, and effect_evidence_sha256 equal to the verified completion-marker SHA-256 for product_terminal or the verified manifest SHA-256 otherwise. The verified reader queries the bound dedicated budget root and requires the exact successful or explicit terminal-failure settlement, matching policy/run/operation/permit/settlement IDs and hashes. Missing, overrun, conflicting, effect_unknown, or reconciliation-required settlement withholds terminal status. Exact settlement replay is allowed; storage publication is not rerun.

PD-23 Cancellation and external effects: cancelled requires acknowledged cooperative cancellation evidence and a terminal marker; cancel_unconfirmed records no hard-stop claim and maps to failure. A live/unacknowledged worker, callable exception after possible effect, remote ambiguity, or pointer/settlement ambiguity is effect_unknown and non-retryable without authoritative reconciliation. P2-012B does not implement process-tree kill, remote cancellation, OS CPU/memory/output isolation, external provider, external solver, or RM-028 evidence implementation.

PD-24 Context and execution lineage: persist only typed scalar ContextBindingV1 and existing execution/phase/report/source commitments already admitted by P2-012A. Recompute manifest approval_lineage_head_sha256, context_lineage_head_sha256, and execution_lineage_head_sha256 from the exact admitted bindings and require their equality to state/report ledgers. ContextEnvelope remains attempt-memory-only-v1; ContextPolicy.expires_at remains provider use-expiry and is never reused as storage retention. Raw ContextEnvelope, canonical_payload, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch, provider input, mutable context, secret, or unrestricted provider output is not a new artifact.

PD-25 Calculator and solver compatibility: terminal read/write validates exact ToolBindingV1 pairs, tool contract/tool version, full ToolResult canonical bytes, numeric_exactness compatibility projection, verification observations and tolerance, model/method, approximation seed/sample/iteration/confidence/error/stopping data, warnings, duration, created UTC, and reproduction command. Inventory UTF-8 ordering is storage-only and FinalReport.tool_results remains execution-ordinal ordered. solver_status must remain status unavailable, empty result, capability.available=false; external_solver, full_nlhe_equilibrium, GTO, equilibrium, exploitability, and exact-range capabilities are not promoted and no such claim is inferred.

PD-26 P2-027A lifecycle hook: classify every admitted payload with the approved local-data policy and store only canonical bounded lifecycle audit metadata as an admitted required payload before completion.json. For product_terminal, retention_started_at equals the exact CompletionMarkerV2.published_at frozen for the transaction and RunVerificationBasis is verified_terminal; classification is the maximum admitted source classification without redaction downgrade. For checkpoint, active or approval-pending protection applies and no terminal retention anchor exists. Reader-derived incomplete, corrupt, orphan, path failure, lineage failure, or encryption mismatch may return a pure quarantine_candidate/manual-review evaluation, but no filesystem action. sensitive persistence still requires verified encryption, restricted persistence is forbidden, and public/internal encryption is not claimed.

PD-27 Security boundary: reuse portable run identity, dedicated-root nonoverlap and ownership, platform-normalized root identity, exact namespace grammar, NFC, ASCII-case alias rejection, reserved-device/extension/trailing-dot/ADS rejection, no absolute/drive/URI/backslash/dot segments, symlink/reparse/hardlink rejection, single-link authority, cross-run and legacy collision scans, canonical duplicate-key rejection, strict version dispatch, and algorithm/domain separation. Reread physical bytes before trust and before pointer CAS. Unkeyed SHA-256 detects corruption/correlation only and does not authenticate a same-privilege malicious writer.

PD-28 Platform/durability claim: supported product behavior is cooperating local-process readers/writers on the existing windows_msvcrt and posix_fcntl adapters. File fsync is required; POSIX directory fsync is required when supported; Windows directory sync records unavailable and does not claim power-loss durability. UNC/SMB/NFS/distributed filesystems, cross-volume rename, hardware cache behavior, malicious same-privilege writer, complete syscall-level TOCTOU prevention, secure erase, and unexecuted OS/Python rows remain UNKNOWN or unsupported. A required platform test row that has not executed cannot be reported as passed.

Existing approval behavior remains compatible and is not strengthened beyond exact lineage correlation.

acceptance_criteria: P2-010B implements only an internal, explicit, revision-only synthesis commit seam. It does not connect ordinary Orchestrator.run, resume, load_report, CLI run/resume/show, AppConfig.runs_dir, or an existing flat-v1 run ID to revision storage, because P2-012A rejects legacy/revision namespace overlap and P2-012B owns product integration.

The integration revalidates the exact P2-010A schema-1.0.0 Synthesis PhaseRequest and PhaseOutcome correlation for run_id, phase_id, attempt_id, context_ids, input_hash, policy_snapshot_hash, output_hash, status, requested_next_state, and artifact intents before any revision-store call; only a succeeded synthesis outcome requesting completed is admitted.

The orchestrator prepares phase-transition-plan-v1 while the machine is in FINAL_SYNTHESIS without mutation. Its frozen canonical JSON data fields are exactly schema_version 1.0.0, run_id, source FINAL_SYNTHESIS, target COMPLETED, literal reason durable synthesis revision committed, event_count, event_prefix_sha256, and plan_sha256. The prefix digest is SHA-256 over the domain bytes poker-phase-transition-event-prefix-v1 followed by one zero byte and compact ensure_ascii=false/sort_keys=true/allow_nan=false JSON for the ordered source/target/reason event list. plan_sha256 is SHA-256 over the analogous poker-phase-transition-plan-v1 zero-byte domain followed by the compact canonical JSON of exactly the preceding seven data fields, excluding plan_sha256. Illegal, stale, non-factory-issued, divergent, wrong-reason, wrong-version, or non-synthesis plans fail closed before publication.

The coordinator binds each admitted non-state artifact intent to an exact canonical payload byte sequence and lowercase SHA-256. A null outcome content hash is deterministically filled in the persisted PhaseBindingV1 snapshot from those admitted bytes; a nonnull hash must already match. The state.json intent remains represented but is not materialized because P2-012A is structural_nonterminal and P2-012B owns durable state checkpoints.

The proposed revision contains the complete P2-012A-admitted source graph needed for the synthesis artifacts and exact typed provenance. PhaseBindingV1, ContextBindingV1, ToolBindingV1, BudgetPolicyBindingV1, SourceBindingV1, approval, report, assignment, tool, run, attempt, policy, and context correlations must replay successfully under the separately approved poker-final-report-artifact-v2 contract. P2-010B itself changes no storage canonical/model/store code or version: final report v1 remains lexical-order plus mandatory-context, while v2 validates one identical input/result binding per execution, unique contiguous projected ordinals, ordinal report order, and exactly zero context only for a trace with no agent reports and no execution records.

The internal frozen phase trace includes the exact Synthesis request/outcome, every contributing ContextBuild request/outcome, every Analysis request/outcome, and every ToolResearch request/outcome with complete ToolExecutionBinding values. The coordinator revalidates phase hashes and correlations, ContextDispatch and envelope integrity/assignment/allowlist/attempt-memory-only policy at the recorded creation boundary, validate_analysis_output, and validate_tool_research_output, derives the persisted PhaseBindingV1 and ContextBindingV1 values from those preimages, and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, self-consistent-hash-only, or cross-trace provenance. Raw ContextEnvelope, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch, provider input, and phase-trace preimages stay in memory and are never passed as revision artifacts.

ToolRequest input bytes, ToolResult bytes, requested/supported/result contract versions, request and result IDs, unique contiguous execution ordinals, phase attempt IDs, source/policy hashes, deterministic calculator evidence, seed/sample/iteration/stopping metadata, warnings, errors, and reproduction metadata come from the complete in-memory ToolResearch trace and admitted canonical artifacts. FinalReport.tool_results remains in execution ordinal order even when result IDs have a different UTF-8 lexical order. The integration does not reconstruct a ToolRequest from only ToolResult, rerun a tool or provider effect, reorder or rewrite report bytes, or rewrite numeric evidence.

Before calling RunRevisionStore.publish, the coordinator applies exact-payload-restricted-secret-scan-v1. Each artifact must be no larger than configured RunRevisionStore.max_artifact_bytes and strict UTF-8; JSON scans every recursively parsed object key and string value, JSONL scans every nonempty line the same way, and Markdown scans the whole decoded text. Object keys use case-insensitive substring regex api[-_]?key|authorization|bearer|cookie|password|passwd|secret|token|private[-_]?key|client[-_]?(secret|credential)|credential. Every string value and Markdown text use the exact case-insensitive union regex from P2-027A storage control metadata: \bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b; \bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b; \bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}\b; \b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}\b; \bAIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\b; \beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\b; \bxox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}\b; \bnpm_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b; \b(?:rk|sk)_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}\b; \bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{8,}\b; and (?:api[-_]?key|password|passwd|secret|token)\s*[:=]. It additionally rejects -----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY----- and case-insensitive \b(?:api[-_]?key|access[-_]?token|password|client[-_]?secret)\b\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?[A-Za-z0-9_./+=-]{12,}. Parse failure, unsupported media/serialization, sensitive/restricted/unknown/downgraded classification, or caller evidence disagreement fails closed.

Every caught coordinator validation, scanner, canonical, and storage Exception is consumed inside a minimal catch boundary and mapped only to a frozen phase-revision-failure-v1 data value with exactly schema_version 1.0.0 and one closed code from invalid_trace, invalid_plan, secret_detected, unsupported_payload, persistence_denied, publish_conflict, publish_uncertain, authorization_mismatch, apply_failed, or apply_unknown. The public coordinator result is a closed success-or-failure data union: phase-revision-failure-v1 is never raised as an exception, contains no exception member, and no caught exception, __cause__, __context__, __traceback__, traceback frame, frame local, raw byte, matched value, ContextEnvelope canonical payload, AgentContext, PhaseRequest/Outcome repr, provider/tool input, or secret crosses or is retained by the seam. The catch boundary emits no raw log or warning and constructs/returns the closed value without embedding or chaining the caught object. Parametrized canaries cover every credential family in innocuous JSON keys, CaseInput.raw_text, nested JSONL, ToolResult, and Markdown with mutation-zero denial; they recursively inspect the returned union, str/repr/log/warning captures, and any exposed object graph to prove that no BaseException, traceback, frame, frame local, canary, or raw payload is reachable.

ContextPolicy and ContextEnvelope remain schema 1.0.0 and attempt-memory-only-v1. Only typed non-secret context identity, classification, source hash, policy hash, lineage, expiry, producer/consumer runtime, envelope hash, and phase input/output hash commitments may persist; provider use-expiry and storage retention remain separate. Provider prompts, ContextEnvelope.canonical_payload, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch objects, provider payloads, and phase trace preimages are never persisted. A clean approved CaseInput raw_text remains an existing input.json/normalized_case.json field and is not mislabelled as a provider prompt. No secret, retention executor, or lifecycle hook is added.

The transaction_id is the stable idempotency key for the whole canonical RevisionPublishRequestV1. Exact replay must reuse the entire request and digest; same transaction with different bytes fails as idempotency_conflict, stale expected revision fails as run_conflict, overlap fails as run_locked, and P2-010B performs zero automatic retry or wait.

The coordinator returns a frozen nonserializable same-process phase-transition-authorization-v1 only after RunRevisionStore.publish returns published or exact current_committed. Its exact data fields are schema_version 1.0.0, plan, run_id_sha256, transaction_id, transaction_sha256, revision, manifest_sha256, pointer_sha256, and outcome_kind published or current_committed, plus one repr-hidden compare-false private issuer-capability identity that is neither a data field nor persistable. A private factory issues it only from one frozen request/plan bundle after matching the complete outcome run hash, transaction identity/digest, revision, manifest, pointer, closed durability/reconciliation matrix, and confirmed authority release; storage does not contain or attest plan_sha256. Apply requires the exact factory-issued capability identity, exact plan self-hash, exact authorization data, the original in-memory bundle identity, and a fresh matching machine preview. historical_committed, reconciliation_required, every RunStorageError, effect_unknown, current_may_have_advanced, release failure, outcome mismatch, reconstructed/reparsed authorization, or any value not issued by that factory returns no authority.

The orchestrator, not the coordinator and not an arbitrary callback, applies an authorized plan through one state-machine lock and a closed applied/already_applied/apply_failed/apply_unknown result. All validation and injected pre-mutation faults occur before replacing the event list and state and return apply_failed; exact event already present returns already_applied; response loss after mutation is reconciled under the same lock to already_applied when exact, otherwise apply_unknown. Exact concurrent replay creates at most one FINAL_SYNTHESIS-to-COMPLETED event, stale/divergent/forged authorization fails closed, and no rollback is claimed.

Fault injection covers forged request/outcome/binding values, secret/classification mismatch, preflight refusal, lock contention and API failure, metadata/namespace/staging/payload/manifest/revision rename faults, CAS and pointer ambiguity, directory-sync failure, lock-release failure, current/historical replay, idempotency payload conflict, orphan/reconciliation outcome, pre-apply and post-observation apply faults, concurrent writer, and concurrent exact replay. No denied or uncertain storage outcome authorizes COMPLETED.

A published structural revision followed by an in-memory apply failure is reported as apply_failed or apply_unknown without rollback or deletion claims. Recovery is limited to exact request replay plus idempotent apply against a matching live machine; process-restart reconstruction, durable resume, terminal visibility, public completed status, migration, and orphan repair remain P2-012B or later.

Windows directory-sync unavailable may authorize a successfully reconciled published outcome only for the tested local cooperating-process visibility contract. P2-010B makes no power-loss, hardware-cache, cross-volume, UNC, SMB, NFS, distributed, malicious-writer, universal directory-durability, or process-crash state-recovery claim.

Ordinary flat-v1 behavior remains byte/order/signature compatible, including Orchestrator.run/resume/load_report, CLI commands and exit codes, CaseInput, FinalReport, ToolResult, serial phase order, golden normalization, calculation assignment artifacts, and the assigned-but-unexecuted report-writer. The characterized flat-v1 COMPLETED-before-final-report-write fault remains explicitly unresolved and is not represented as fixed by this opt-in seam.

P2-010A phase contracts remain versioned internal APIs and are not exported as stable package-root APIs. Pure phases still do no filesystem, state-machine, provider, tool, network, approval-ledger, ambient-clock, or ambient-random mutation; provider and tool effects remain behind their existing executors, and only the orchestrator may request or apply a transition.

Execution remains serial with zero automatic retries and peak concurrency one. P2-010B does not add durable usage, reservation, multi-process budget CAS, retry scheduling, parallel agents, cancellation fan-out, provider execution, external solver execution, runtime bridges, sandboxing, or approval CAS, and it does not change budget observation or settlement semantics.

P2-010B accepts only poker-final-report-artifact-v2 on a dedicated revision root whose ownership marker exactly matches RunRevisionStore producer_id p2-010b-phase-revision and producer_version 0.2.0. Before the target run's initial publication, inspection must prove that target run has no current pointer or revision history; histories for other run IDs are outside this check. After a published revision exists, only an explicit same-process replay of the original frozen request/plan bundle whose run, transaction, transaction digest, revision, manifest, and pointer exactly produce current_committed is exempt; different transaction, historical, successor, reconstructed, or cross-process replay is denied. Same-canonical-build, no-mixed-build, and no-rolling access are trusted deployment assumptions which the unchanged schemas cannot attest, detect, or prevent, so violation is unsupported rather than claimed to fail closed. Producer mismatch, nonexact target-run history, v1 final report, or old reader fails; new readers retain v1 read support, old readers reject explicit v2, and no cross-build availability, migration, rewrite, or conversion claim is made.

Capabilities, doctor, README, architecture, phase, storage, security, context, budget, tool, limitation, and generated roadmap docs state the narrow internal structural integration and separately approved final-report artifact v2 boundary truthfully. immutable_revision_storage_foundation stays implemented; product_integrated_durable_run stays planned; no GTO, equilibrium, exploitability, exact-range, external-provider, external-solver, parallel, retry, terminal, resume, migration, cleanup, encryption, or secure-erase capability is promoted.

After the separately approved split-milestone governance and final-report artifact v2 amendments, roadmap sequencing is append-only: scope freeze binds this exact scope and post-approval digest while P2-010B remains not_started and RM-010 remains in_progress; implementation start changes only P2-010B to in_progress; completion changes P2-010B and RM-010 to completed with exact approved path/test evidence. P2-011B and P2-012B remain approval null and not_started.

Candidate and exact-final-HEAD gates run every approved test plus full pytest, ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy src, roadmap generate/check --require-tracked, doctor JSON, management JSON/JSONL validation, ignore/untracked/nonstage guards, git diff --check, and four independent reviews. Completion evidence is created only after candidate High=0 and Medium=0, and push occurs only after final High=0 and Medium=0 with every Low fixed or concretely accepted.

The branch is created only after explicit approval of all three proposals and baseline revalidation. Commits are separated into split-milestone governance amendment, final-report artifact v2 amendment, P2-010B scope freeze, implementation start, coordinator/state contract, orchestrator integration, fault/concurrency/security remediation, docs/review remediation, and completion evidence; only exact phase-specific allowlisted paths are staged, push is non-force, and ignored management data remains untracked, unstaged, uncommitted, unpushed, untransmitted, and undeleted.

Implement P2-010B only; do not implement P2-011B, P2-012B, P2-013A/B, P2-027B, P2-028A, or later work. Record P2-011B only as the next proposal-only handoff in ignored management data after P2-010B completion.

Resolve the legacy/revision namespace conflict by choosing an internal explicit revision-only synthesis commit seam. Do not dual-write a normal flat-v1 run, use a different run ID to evade binding, alter the P2-012A namespace refusal, or connect run/resume/show before P2-012B.

Add phases/revision_coordinator.py as an internal module without package-root or phases.__init__ export. Preserve P2-010A and P2-012A schema versions and do not modify revision_models.py, revision_canonical.py, revision_lock.py, revision_store.py, run_store.py, config.py, cli.py, phases/contracts.py, phases/models.py, phases/services.py, or phases/executors.py in P2-010B. The separately approved final-report artifact v2 amendment must be completed first.

The revision coordinator accepts an orchestrator-owned frozen trace of already-computed ContextBuild, Analysis, ToolResearch, and Synthesis strict request/outcome values plus a complete canonical revision request; it performs preimage correlation, exact-byte classification, materialized-intent, canonical, outcome, and authorization validation around RunRevisionStore.publish. It may rerun pure validation functions but never reruns a provider/tool effect, invokes a state transition or filesystem callback, starts a retry loop, performs cleanup, or accepts an arbitrary mutation callback.

Only Synthesis with status succeeded and requested_next_state completed can produce a transition plan or authorization. completed_with_failures, failed, missing output, non-synthesis phase, null/other target, schema mismatch, hash mismatch, warning-based policy violation, or any forged correlation fails closed.

Represent the pending state change as phase-transition-plan-v1 with the exact serialized data fields, literal reason durable synthesis revision committed, domain-separated compact canonical event-prefix and plan hashes fixed in the acceptance criteria. Preview is pure. The nonserializable same-process phase-transition-authorization-v1 has the exact frozen data fields and repr-hidden private factory capability fixed in the acceptance criteria; it correlates the original in-memory request/plan bundle to exact publication identities without claiming that storage attests plan_sha256. Apply is orchestrator-owned, lock-serialized, idempotent, rejects non-factory-issued, reconstructed, tampered, stale, or mismatched values, and emits no duplicate event.

Persist no state.json payload, completion marker, terminal manifest/pointer, verified product status, resume checkpoint, migration record, retention anchor, or lifecycle action. The PhaseBindingV1 may retain the exact state intent identity while canonical storage continues to skip state intent materialization.

For every non-state intent, compute content_sha256 from the exact admitted canonical bytes. Preserve any correct nonnull phase hash, reject disagreement, and deterministically materialize a null phase hash in the persisted binding; do not accept an intent without its required payload or an admitted payload outside the declared source graph.

Require the separately approved poker-final-report-artifact-v2 canonical validator to replay the complete provenance graph and preserve v1 semantics separately. For v2, project one exact identical input/result ToolBinding per execution, require ordinals 0 through n-1, compare report results by ordinal, and require context if and only if provider reports/execution records exist. Correlate run, revision, transaction, phase, attempt, context, policy, assignment, agent execution, tool request/result, report, evidence, approval, source, and budget identities without byte rewrite.

Carry exact ContextBuild, Analysis, ToolResearch, and Synthesis PhaseRequest/PhaseOutcome preimages in a frozen internal trace. Revalidate ContextDispatch, assignment_sha256, ContextEnvelope integrity/policy/payload/source hashes, attempt identity, allowlist/blind isolation, Analysis output, ToolExecutionBinding, and phase hashes before deriving persisted hash-only bindings. Reject missing/extra/cross-run/cross-attempt or hash-only forged provenance; never persist the raw trace.

Carry complete ToolExecutionBinding values before any projection to ToolResult. Preserve exact canonical ToolRequest input and ToolResult bytes, require exactly one identical binding across each input/result pair, project one binding per execution, require unique contiguous ordinals 0 through n-1, and preserve all reproduction metadata; never infer missing request fields from a result, reorder FinalReport.tool_results, or rerun a calculator or solver.

Use exact-payload-restricted-secret-scan-v1 before building P2-027A classification evidence: scan at most configured max_artifact_bytes per artifact; decode strict UTF-8; recursively scan every JSON/JSONL object key and string value and all Markdown text; implement the complete exact P2-027A/storage-control GitHub, AWS, Google, JWT, Slack, npm, Stripe, OpenAI-style, Bearer, assignment, access-token/client-secret, and PEM private-key families fixed in the acceptance criteria. Clean internal/public is the only persistable result; detected secret, sensitive/restricted/unknown classification, caller evidence disagreement, parse failure, unsupported serialization/media, or over-limit input is a mutation-zero prepublish denial.

Catch every raw-trace, scanner, canonical, and storage Exception at a minimal internal boundary and return only the phase-revision-failure-v1 closed redacted data union; never raise that failure value or return, attach, chain, log, warn, or retain any exception object. Never expose or retain a raw trace, matched secret, canonical payload, tool/provider input, underlying ValidationError repr, __cause__, __context__, __traceback__, traceback frame/local, BaseException, or canary in str/repr/results/logs/warnings/fault output or any reachable returned object graph; adversarial tests cover every credential family and failure surface.

Keep ContextEnvelope/ContextPolicy 1.0.0, attempt-memory-only-v1, fresh attempt identity, blind isolation, classification/source/policy hashes, lineage, expiry, and producer/consumer runtime semantics. Persist derived hashes and typed provenance only, never ContextEnvelope.canonical_payload, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch/provider payload, or phase-trace preimages. Existing clean CaseInput raw_text in approved run input artifacts remains permitted and is not a provider prompt.

Use the RevisionPublishRequestV1 transaction_id and canonical transaction digest as the idempotency identity. Allow no automatic retry even when a failure is semantically retryable; expose deterministic failure/uncertainty to the caller. The only admitted explicit replay is the original same-process frozen request/plan bundle and may authorize only exact current_committed; process-restart reconstruction or a newly previewed plan is denied and remains a non-goal.

Authorize only published or exact current_committed after all outcome fields, current identity, reconciliation, durability contract, and lock release are confirmed. Deny historical_committed, reconciliation_required, RunStorageError, effect_unknown, current_may_have_advanced, release failure, outcome mismatch, or any response outside the closed allowlist.

Treat Windows directory_sync unavailable as successful only where the existing published outcome contract permits it and document the limited local cooperating-process visibility. Make no power-loss, network filesystem, distributed, malicious writer, or restart-resume guarantee.

The failure matrix is closed: pure validation and secret/classification failures are mutation-zero; lock contention/API failure, quota, CAS, idempotency conflict, metadata, namespace, staging, payload, manifest, rename, pointer, directory-sync, release, historical replay, orphan, and reconciliation outcomes never authorize transition unless the exact published/current_committed allowlist is satisfied.

The recovery matrix is closed: prepublish failure leaves no transition; partial/unreferenced writes remain P2-012A-described orphans; uncertain current/release outcomes require reconciliation and no transition; pre-apply fault leaves a committed structural revision and a non-COMPLETED live machine; exact current replay can reauthorize and idempotently apply; durable restart, public status, repair, rollback, delete, and migration are non-goals.

The concurrency matrix is closed: one nonblocking revision writer may publish, overlapping writers receive RunLocked or a deterministic conflict, stale expected values receive RunConflict, exact concurrent replay can yield current_committed but at most one matching state event, and no scheduling parallelism or wait loop is introduced.

Preserve normal Orchestrator.run/resume/load_report and CLI signatures, output meanings, flat-v1 layout and artifact write order, golden behavior, calculation assignment artifact, and assigned-but-unexecuted report-writer. Normal flat-v1 bytes are not silently adopted, copied, deleted, migrated, or dual-written.

Explicitly retain the known flat-v1 fault in which COMPLETED/state can precede a later final-report write failure. P2-010B proves no-COMPLETED-on-failure only for its opt-in revision-only seam and must not overstate ordinary product atomicity.

Keep phase contracts internal, serial execution, zero automatic retries, peak concurrency one, in-memory budget usage, current cancellation behavior, provider/tool effect ownership, blind isolation, and orchestrator-only transition ownership unchanged.

Do not add or promote external provider, external solver, full NLHE equilibrium, GTO, exploitability, exact-range, parallel agent, automatic retry, durable budget, approval authority, terminal run, verified reader, resume, migration, lifecycle cleanup, encryption, secure erase, sandbox, or runtime-bridge capability.

acceptance_criteria: P2-010B implements only an internal, explicit, revision-only synthesis commit seam. It does not connect ordinary Orchestrator.run, resume, load_report, CLI run/resume/show, AppConfig.runs_dir, or an existing flat-v1 run ID to revision storage, because P2-012A rejects legacy/revision namespace overlap and P2-012B owns product integration.

The integration revalidates the exact P2-010A schema-1.0.0 Synthesis PhaseRequest and PhaseOutcome correlation for run_id, phase_id, attempt_id, context_ids, input_hash, policy_snapshot_hash, output_hash, status, requested_next_state, and artifact intents before any revision-store call; only a succeeded synthesis outcome requesting completed is admitted.

The orchestrator prepares phase-transition-plan-v1 while the machine is in FINAL_SYNTHESIS without mutation. Its frozen canonical JSON data fields are exactly schema_version 1.0.0, run_id, source FINAL_SYNTHESIS, target COMPLETED, literal reason durable synthesis revision committed, event_count, event_prefix_sha256, and plan_sha256. The prefix digest is SHA-256 over the domain bytes poker-phase-transition-event-prefix-v1 followed by one zero byte and compact ensure_ascii=false/sort_keys=true/allow_nan=false JSON for the ordered source/target/reason event list. plan_sha256 is SHA-256 over the analogous poker-phase-transition-plan-v1 zero-byte domain followed by the compact canonical JSON of exactly the preceding seven data fields, excluding plan_sha256. Illegal, stale, non-factory-issued, divergent, wrong-reason, wrong-version, or non-synthesis plans fail closed before publication.

The coordinator binds each admitted non-state artifact intent to an exact canonical payload byte sequence and lowercase SHA-256. A null outcome content hash is deterministically filled in the persisted PhaseBindingV1 snapshot from those admitted bytes; a nonnull hash must already match. The state.json intent remains represented but is not materialized because P2-012A is structural_nonterminal and P2-012B owns durable state checkpoints.

The proposed revision contains the complete P2-012A-admitted source graph needed for the synthesis artifacts and exact typed provenance. PhaseBindingV1, ContextBindingV1, ToolBindingV1, BudgetPolicyBindingV1, SourceBindingV1, approval, report, assignment, tool, run, attempt, policy, and context correlations must replay successfully under the separately approved poker-final-report-artifact-v2 contract. P2-010B itself changes no storage canonical/model/store code or version: final report v1 remains lexical-order plus mandatory-context, while v2 validates one identical input/result binding per execution, unique contiguous projected ordinals, ordinal report order, and exactly zero context only for a trace with no agent reports and no execution records.

The internal frozen phase trace includes the exact Synthesis request/outcome, every contributing ContextBuild request/outcome, every Analysis request/outcome, and every ToolResearch request/outcome with complete ToolExecutionBinding values. The coordinator revalidates phase hashes and correlations, ContextDispatch and envelope integrity/assignment/allowlist/attempt-memory-only policy at the recorded creation boundary, validate_analysis_output, and validate_tool_research_output, derives the persisted PhaseBindingV1 and ContextBindingV1 values from those preimages, and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, self-consistent-hash-only, or cross-trace provenance. Raw ContextEnvelope, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch, provider input, and phase-trace preimages stay in memory and are never passed as revision artifacts.

ToolRequest input bytes, ToolResult bytes, requested/supported/result contract versions, request and result IDs, unique contiguous execution ordinals, phase attempt IDs, source/policy hashes, deterministic calculator evidence, seed/sample/iteration/stopping metadata, warnings, errors, and reproduction metadata come from the complete in-memory ToolResearch trace and admitted canonical artifacts. FinalReport.tool_results remains in execution ordinal order even when result IDs have a different UTF-8 lexical order. The integration does not reconstruct a ToolRequest from only ToolResult, rerun a tool or provider effect, reorder or rewrite report bytes, or rewrite numeric evidence.

Before calling RunRevisionStore.publish, the coordinator applies exact-payload-restricted-secret-scan-v1. Each artifact must be no larger than configured RunRevisionStore.max_artifact_bytes and strict UTF-8; JSON scans every recursively parsed object key and string value, JSONL scans every nonempty line the same way, and Markdown scans the whole decoded text. Object keys use case-insensitive substring regex api[-_]?key|authorization|bearer|cookie|password|passwd|secret|token|private[-_]?key|client[-_]?(secret|credential)|credential. Every string value and Markdown text use the exact case-insensitive union regex from P2-027A storage control metadata: \bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b; \bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b; \bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}\b; \b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}\b; \bAIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\b; \beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\b; \bxox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}\b; \bnpm_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b; \b(?:rk|sk)_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}\b; \bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{8,}\b; and (?:api[-_]?key|password|passwd|secret|token)\s*[:=]. It additionally rejects -----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY----- and case-insensitive \b(?:api[-_]?key|access[-_]?token|password|client[-_]?secret)\b\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?[A-Za-z0-9_./+=-]{12,}. Parse failure, unsupported media/serialization, sensitive/restricted/unknown/downgraded classification, or caller evidence disagreement fails closed.

Every caught coordinator validation, scanner, canonical, and storage Exception is consumed inside a minimal catch boundary and mapped only to a frozen phase-revision-failure-v1 data value with exactly schema_version 1.0.0 and one closed code from invalid_trace, invalid_plan, secret_detected, unsupported_payload, persistence_denied, publish_conflict, publish_uncertain, authorization_mismatch, apply_failed, or apply_unknown. The public coordinator result is a closed success-or-failure data union: phase-revision-failure-v1 is never raised as an exception, contains no exception member, and no caught exception, __cause__, __context__, __traceback__, traceback frame, frame local, raw byte, matched value, ContextEnvelope canonical payload, AgentContext, PhaseRequest/Outcome repr, provider/tool input, or secret crosses or is retained by the seam. The catch boundary emits no raw log or warning and constructs/returns the closed value without embedding or chaining the caught object. Parametrized canaries cover every credential family in innocuous JSON keys, CaseInput.raw_text, nested JSONL, ToolResult, and Markdown with mutation-zero denial; they recursively inspect the returned union, str/repr/log/warning captures, and any exposed object graph to prove that no BaseException, traceback, frame, frame local, canary, or raw payload is reachable.

ContextPolicy and ContextEnvelope remain schema 1.0.0 and attempt-memory-only-v1. Only typed non-secret context identity, classification, source hash, policy hash, lineage, expiry, producer/consumer runtime, envelope hash, and phase input/output hash commitments may persist; provider use-expiry and storage retention remain separate. Provider prompts, ContextEnvelope.canonical_payload, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch objects, provider payloads, and phase trace preimages are never persisted. A clean approved CaseInput raw_text remains an existing input.json/normalized_case.json field and is not mislabelled as a provider prompt. No secret, retention executor, or lifecycle hook is added.

The transaction_id is the stable idempotency key for the whole canonical RevisionPublishRequestV1. Exact replay must reuse the entire request and digest; same transaction with different bytes fails as idempotency_conflict, stale expected revision fails as run_conflict, overlap fails as run_locked, and P2-010B performs zero automatic retry or wait.

The coordinator returns a frozen nonserializable same-process phase-transition-authorization-v1 only after RunRevisionStore.publish returns published or exact current_committed. Its exact data fields are schema_version 1.0.0, plan, run_id_sha256, transaction_id, transaction_sha256, revision, manifest_sha256, pointer_sha256, and outcome_kind published or current_committed, plus one repr-hidden compare-false private issuer-capability identity that is neither a data field nor persistable. A private factory issues it only from one frozen request/plan bundle after matching the complete outcome run hash, transaction identity/digest, revision, manifest, pointer, closed durability/reconciliation matrix, and confirmed authority release; storage does not contain or attest plan_sha256. Apply requires the exact factory-issued capability identity, exact plan self-hash, exact authorization data, the original in-memory bundle identity, and a fresh matching machine preview. historical_committed, reconciliation_required, every RunStorageError, effect_unknown, current_may_have_advanced, release failure, outcome mismatch, reconstructed/reparsed authorization, or any value not issued by that factory returns no authority.

The orchestrator, not the coordinator and not an arbitrary callback, applies an authorized plan through one state-machine lock and a closed applied/already_applied/apply_failed/apply_unknown result. All validation and injected pre-mutation faults occur before replacing the event list and state and return apply_failed; exact event already present returns already_applied; response loss after mutation is reconciled under the same lock to already_applied when exact, otherwise apply_unknown.
